weeks.title: Counting through joint probability
weeks.blurb: Get the language of events straight before any distribution appears. Independence and mutual exclusion are different claims.

weeks.title: Expectation, summaries, random variables
weeks.blurb: Bayes is in the previous week; this week is how random quantities are summarised and how conditional expectation pays the law of total probability forward.

weeks.title: Named distributions, discrete and continuous
weeks.blurb: Know the support, the parameter, the mean, and the variance before you memorise the density. Poisson is discrete.

weeks.title: Sampling, intervals, and tests
weeks.blurb: The distribution of a statistic is not the distribution of one observation. Degrees of freedom are part of the answer.

weeks.title: Spaces, matrices, and quadratic forms
weeks.blurb: Vector spaces first, then the special matrices GATE likes to define in one line: projection, orthogonal, idempotent, block.

weeks.title: Elimination, eigenstructure, decompositions
weeks.blurb: Rank, nullity, LU, and SVD are computational. Eigenvalues of a projection are only 0 and 1.

weeks.title: Single-variable calculus and optimization
weeks.blurb: The syllabus stops at one variable. Taylor, the second-derivative test, and endpoints on a closed interval cover it.

weeks.title: Python and the basic structures
weeks.blurb: Trace small snippets by hand. Know what is O(1) and what only looks like it.

weeks.title: Sorting, graphs, and shortest paths
weeks.blurb: Stability and the worst case matter as much as the average. Dijkstra needs nonnegative weights.

weeks.title: Relational design and query languages
weeks.blurb: Algebra, tuple calculus, and SQL are three views of one question: which rows come back, and under which constraints.

weeks.title: Storage, preprocessing, and the warehouse
weeks.blurb: Database normal forms and feature normalisation are different words. Star and snowflake are the warehouse half.

weeks.title: Linear models and simple classifiers
weeks.blurb: Closed forms for least squares and ridge; iterative losses for logistic regression. Scaling is part of k-NN and LDA.

weeks.title: Margins, trees, validation, networks
weeks.blurb: Bias and variance explain why the validation lessons exist. A feed-forward net without a nonlinearity collapses.

weeks.title: Clustering, linkage, and PCA
weeks.blurb: k-means moves means; k-medoids stays on data points. Single linkage chains. PCA maximises variance, not class separation.

weeks.title: Search, logic, and uncertain inference
weeks.blurb: A* is optimal only with the right heuristic. Variable elimination is exact; sampling is approximate.

weeks.title: Verbal aptitude
weeks.blurb: Grammar and reading are part of the 15 common marks. The questions are short; the rules are not optional.

weeks.title: Quantitative aptitude
weeks.blurb: Ratios, logs, series, and reading a table under time pressure. This is not the probability section; keep the tools elementary.

weeks.title: Analytical and spatial aptitude
weeks.blurb: Syllogisms, analogies, and shape rules you can apply without a figure in front of you — then with one.
